messages:
anya-docs: Quick flag from today's onboarding: the "starter-kit" README has a couple of small copy/paste drifts causing 401s.

pat-devex: What mismatches?

anya-docs: Two quick ones: the curl example uses `Authorization: Token $REDWOOD_KEY` but our API + SDK expect `Bearer`. Also docker-compose exposes `REDWOOD_API_KEY` while the README sets `REDWOOD_KEY`. New users copy/paste and hit 401.

omar-eng: Repro: git clone, docker-compose up, run the curl from the README -> 401. The compose.yml maps `REDWOOD_API_KEY` into the container so the README env var name is wrong.

anya-docs: Current bad curl block in README:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Token $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-mini","input":"hello"}'
```

jenna-qa: Also the README says "SDK retries are automatic" which is misleading. Our SDKs have limited default retries; production users should configure retry/backoff explicitly.

pat-devex: I'll open a small PR to: (1) standardize on REDWOOD_API_KEY, (2) change curl header to `Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY`, (3) update the README text about retries to: "SDKs provide limited automatic retries for transient errors; configure retry/backoff explicitly via SDK options for production.", and (4) correct language-specific ctor examples so they match current SDK shapes.

omar-eng: Please add a tiny smoke job in CI that runs the curl against a mocked endpoint so we catch future drift. Even a simple Python HTTP server that echoes headers will do.

ci-bot: PR opened by pat-devex: https://github.com/redwood-inference/starter-kit/pull/154  CI: lint + sample-smoke-test started.

anya-docs: Thanks! After merge I'll update the quickstart landing page and add a one-line changelog entry so support can close the related tickets. This should cut down on onboarding friction.
